sources.pickup_handling_min: PLACEHOLDER: team assumption, chosen so the reference shipment S-01 departs 10:00
sources.mpg: San Pedro Bay Ports (Los Angeles and Long Beach), 2021 Update: Feasibility Assessment for Drayage Trucks, February 2023, p. 71: port truck operators reported an average diesel fuel economy of 6.8 miles per gallon in the 2021 Clean Trucks Program survey. Reported by fleets, not measured on the road.
sources.nonlabor_cost_per_mile: American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI), An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking: 2026 Update (2025 data), line items as reported by FleetOwner on 22 July 2026: $2.336 per mile in total, less driver wages ($0.818) and benefits ($0.210). What remains is fuel ($0.482), truck and trailer payments ($0.40), repair and maintenance ($0.22), insurance ($0.11), tires ($0.05), tolls ($0.043) and permits ($0.008). A national average for all trucking, not specific to drayage or to California.
sources.labor_rate_per_hr: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025: annual mean wage of $59,710 for heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers, which is $28.71 an hour over 2,080 hours. Benefits are added at the ratio in ATRI's 2026 Update ($0.210 of benefits for each $0.818 of wages). A national average for employed drivers.
sources.diesel_kgCO2_per_gal: U.S. EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub, 2025 edition (Emission Factors for Greenhouse Gas Inventories, last modified 15 January 2025), Table 2 Mobile Combustion CO2: diesel fuel, 10.21 kg CO2 per gallon. Tailpipe CO2 only.
